display_name: Vasse Felix Filius Cabernet Sauvignon, Margaret River
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "A straight-up Margaret River Cabernet priced for everyday drinking, the Filius bottling leans on cool maritime influence and gravelly soils to deliver dark fruit and a savory, slightly minty edge. It’s the accessible Cabernet from a founding Margaret River house, built to be immediate rather than archival.",
  "wine_summary": "This Filius Cabernet Sauvignon is Vasse Felix’s entry-level single-varietal Cab from Margaret River, offering a focused expression of the region’s blackcurrant and eucalyptus notes at a sub-$30 price point. Vasse Felix helped define Margaret River’s international reputation for Cabernet; the Filius line distills that lineage into a wine shaped by well-draining red gravelly loam and loamy gravel over clay soils that concentrate fruit while retaining enough moisture for balanced ripeness. Tasting notes — kirsch, cassis, tobacco, and a marine-savory lift — tie directly to the estate’s maritime climate and iron-rich pockets that give Cabernet an herbaceous-mineral streak here.",
  "terroir_expression": "Margaret River sits on a narrow coastal strip with a Mediterranean, maritime climate moderated by the Indian Ocean; cooling sea breezes and relatively mild winters slow ripening, preserving acidity and aromatics. Soils in the GI range from red gravelly loam and loamy gravel over clay to deep infertile sands and Forest Grove ironstone; for Cabernet, the gravel and ironstone parcels force vines to work, producing concentrated black-fruit flavors, firm phenolics and a saline-mineral lift that reads as minty or nori-like in the glass.",
  "vinification_summary": "Public technical notes for Filius are limited, so inferred winemaking leans toward practices aimed at approachability: controlled extraction to retain plush mid-palate fruit, followed by some oak maturation to soften tannins and add spice components (oak maturation means aging in wood to developmentally integrate tannin and flavour). Those choices explain the wine’s dense dark-fruit core, moderate acidity and savory spice hints rather than aggressive new-oak signatures.",
  "food_pairing": "Nashville hot chicken (casual) — the wine’s acidity and firm tannins tame the fried fat while dark fruit offsets the spicy heat.\nSlow-roasted lamb shoulder with rosemary and garlic (family-style) — cassis and savory tobacco notes echo the roast’s herb and gamy flavors; tannins cut the fat.\nCharred eggplant with miso glaze and sesame (vegetarian, bistro) — the wine’s umami/mineral thread matches miso, while fruit keeps the dish from feeling bitter.\nAged English cheddar and quince paste (cheese course) — dense dark fruit and structured tannins stand up to fat and salt, and the quince lifts the wine’s fruit.\nSeared New York strip with peppercorn jus (fine dining) — concentrated fruit and mid-weight tannin support beef and the wine’s savory spice complements the jus.",
  "comparable_wines": "Cape Mentelle Cabernet Sauvignon — why it's comparable: another Margaret River Cabernet that balances blackcurrant fruit with coastal herbal notes and sits in the same everyday-premium price band.\nWynns Coonawarra Estate Cabernet Sauvignon — why it's comparable: Coonawarra Cabernets show similar cassis and eucalyptus/menthol lift with firm tannins at a similar retail price, offering a good point of comparison for Old-World-structured Australian Cabernets.",
  "style_profile": "Cabernet Sauvignon-based full-bodied dry red with firm tannins and a savory-mineral streak",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink within the next 1–8 years; store at 12–14°C with moderate humidity and keep bottles on their sides. It rewards short-term cellaring but is not built for multi-decade aging.",
  "value_assessment": "Price: $26.31. At this price the Filius delivers clear Margaret River Cabernet character—black currant, dark cherry and savory herb—against competitors like Cape Mentelle Cabernet (roughly $30) and Wynns Coonawarra Cabernet (~$25–30). It’s worth buying if you want regionally specific Cabernet without paying estate-level prices; quality-to-price is strong for retail and casual restaurant lists.",
  "market_position": "This wine sits on casual-to-smart-retail shelves and in bistro lists where buyers want a recognizable Australian Cabernet under $30. It appeals to diners ordering steak or roast at mid-priced restaurants, retail shoppers seeking a dependable Margaret River label, and trade buyers who need consistent house-Cabernet presence rather than collectible bottlings.",
  "insider_take": "Think of Filius as a value-forward Margaret River Cabernet: it gives regional signatures—gravel-driven concentration, minty/savory lift—without the tannic backbone or oak complexity collectors chase. Buy it for everyday drinking, food service rotation and casual entertaining; skip it if you need a Cabernet for long-term investment or trophy bottles.",

parsed.wine_summary: This Filius Cabernet Sauvignon is Vasse Felix’s entry-level single-varietal Cab from Margaret River, offering a focused expression of the region’s blackcurrant and eucalyptus notes at a sub-$30 price point. Vasse Felix helped define Margaret River’s international reputation for Cabernet; the Filius line distills that lineage into a wine shaped by well-draining red gravelly loam and loamy gravel over clay soils that concentrate fruit while retaining enough moisture for balanced ripeness. Tasting notes — kirsch, cassis, tobacco, and a marine-savory lift — tie directly to the estate’s maritime climate and iron-rich pockets that give Cabernet an herbaceous-mineral streak here.
parsed.terroir_expression: Margaret River sits on a narrow coastal strip with a Mediterranean, maritime climate moderated by the Indian Ocean; cooling sea breezes and relatively mild winters slow ripening, preserving acidity and aromatics. Soils in the GI range from red gravelly loam and loamy gravel over clay to deep infertile sands and Forest Grove ironstone; for Cabernet, the gravel and ironstone parcels force vines to work, producing concentrated black-fruit flavors, firm phenolics and a saline-mineral lift that reads as minty or nori-like in the glass.
parsed.vinification_summary: Public technical notes for Filius are limited, so inferred winemaking leans toward practices aimed at approachability: controlled extraction to retain plush mid-palate fruit, followed by some oak maturation to soften tannins and add spice components (oak maturation means aging in wood to developmentally integrate tannin and flavour). Those choices explain the wine’s dense dark-fruit core, moderate acidity and savory spice hints rather than aggressive new-oak signatures.
parsed.food_pairing:
Nashville hot chicken (casual) — the wine’s acidity and firm tannins tame the fried fat while dark fruit offsets the spicy heat.
Slow-roasted lamb shoulder with rosemary and garlic (family-style) — cassis and savory tobacco notes echo the roast’s herb and gamy flavors; tannins cut the fat.
Charred eggplant with miso glaze and sesame (vegetarian, bistro) — the wine’s umami/mineral thread matches miso, while fruit keeps the dish from feeling bitter.
Aged English cheddar and quince paste (cheese course) — dense dark fruit and structured tannins stand up to fat and salt, and the quince lifts the wine’s fruit.
Seared New York strip with peppercorn jus (fine dining) — concentrated fruit and mid-weight tannin support beef and the wine’s savory spice complements the jus.
parsed.comparable_wines:
Cape Mentelle Cabernet Sauvignon — why it's comparable: another Margaret River Cabernet that balances blackcurrant fruit with coastal herbal notes and sits in the same everyday-premium price band.
Wynns Coonawarra Estate Cabernet Sauvignon — why it's comparable: Coonawarra Cabernets show similar cassis and eucalyptus/menthol lift with firm tannins at a similar retail price, offering a good point of comparison for Old-World-structured Australian Cabernets.
parsed.style_profile: Cabernet Sauvignon-based full-bodied dry red with firm tannins and a savory-mineral streak
parsed.cellar_recommendation: Drink within the next 1–8 years; store at 12–14°C with moderate humidity and keep bottles on their sides. It rewards short-term cellaring but is not built for multi-decade aging.
parsed.value_assessment: Price: $26.31. At this price the Filius delivers clear Margaret River Cabernet character—black currant, dark cherry and savory herb—against competitors like Cape Mentelle Cabernet (roughly $30) and Wynns Coonawarra Cabernet (~$25–30). It’s worth buying if you want regionally specific Cabernet without paying estate-level prices; quality-to-price is strong for retail and casual restaurant lists.
parsed.market_position: This wine sits on casual-to-smart-retail shelves and in bistro lists where buyers want a recognizable Australian Cabernet under $30. It appeals to diners ordering steak or roast at mid-priced restaurants, retail shoppers seeking a dependable Margaret River label, and trade buyers who need consistent house-Cabernet presence rather than collectible bottlings.
parsed.insider_take: Think of Filius as a value-forward Margaret River Cabernet: it gives regional signatures—gravel-driven concentration, minty/savory lift—without the tannic backbone or oak complexity collectors chase. Buy it for everyday drinking, food service rotation and casual entertaining; skip it if you need a Cabernet for long-term investment or trophy bottles.
